human_tolerance.notes: Uses towns, buildings, and garden food sources, but remains more wary in rural settings. The broad urban affinity and model parameters are judgement; no flight-distance figure is asserted.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: UK birds are resident year-round; pair bonds persist outside the breeding season.

vocalizations.description: A metallic, squeaky chyak-chyak or kak-kak contact call, often given in flight.
A hoarse, drawn-out arrrrr or kaaaarr call warns flock-mates about predators and can precede mobbing.

taxonomy.note: GBIF provider match returned exact accepted species Coloeus monedula, rank SPECIES; ITIS returns the same name and authority.

external.note: GBIF 6100954, iNaturalist 336399 (active species), and ITIS 916629 checked at their respective providers on 2026-10-31; Wikidata Q25345384 also records the iNaturalist identifier.

common_names.note: ITIS lists Eurasian Jackdaw and Western Jackdaw as English common names; Wikidata and Wikipedia agree on alternate naming.

range.note: The species occurs widely across Europe, western Asia, and western North Africa. This record lists only native GB because issue 502 requests GB activity; it is a region-scoped record, not a complete global range list.

traits.limb_count.note: Two walking legs; wings are excluded by the schema's bird convention.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Describes brisk ground walking and powered flight.

traits.nest_type.note: Nests in cavities in trees, cliffs, and buildings.

traits.size_class.note: Small is the schema class for animals below 1 kg; mass_kg is 0.246.

traits.mass_kg.note: BirdFuncDat row 8073: BodyMass-Value 246 g; converted to 0.246 kg. The dataset's name is Corvus monedula, a synonym of the accepted Coloeus monedula.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the published 34-39 cm length range: (34+39)/2 cm = 36.5 cm = 0.365 m.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Median lifespan about 5.5 years for breeding birds in one wild Groningen population; used as a population-specific proxy for typical wild lifespan.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits row 8073 percentages: invertebrates 30, endothermic vertebrates 10, fruit 30, seeds 30; mapped to the schema categories.

traits.social.note: Flock structure is documented; group size [2,20] is a coarse simulation judgement, not an observed flock-size interval.

traits.defense.note: Flock members use alarm calls and mob predators.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from its reported wariness in rural settings and greater tameness in urban areas; 0.35 is a simulation parameter, not a measured distance.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits row 8073: ground 50%, understory 20%, mid-high 20%, canopy 10%; map ground to ground and all above-ground strata to arboreal.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Perch is a coarse simulation shelter tag for birds that roost communally at elevated sites.

habitat.resources.note: Food and cavity nesting resources reflect the documented diet and cavity nest sites. Equal resource weights are a simulation default, not measured diet proportions.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Adapter judgement based on use of towns, buildings, and urban food sources with greater wariness in rural settings.

seasonal.strategy.note: Mostly resident; northern and eastern populations migrate, while UK birds are resident year-round.

seasonal.phases.note: Year-round territorial phase reflects persistent pair bonds.

behavior.note: Authored overrides to the shared ground-foraging bird program. Invertebrate feeding is represented; seed, fruit, flock coordination, and cavity construction detail are simplified. Nest months 3 and 4 are judgement for the GB simulation.

look.note: Judgement from the black cap/body, grey nape, and pale iris; proportions and block geometry are authored for the preview model.
